content:
I notice that set image has the '' notation (f '' s = s.image f), but Finset doesn't have the same notation. What are usual ways for such situations?

  • add one in finset, and each file need to import exactly one? (seem problematic)
  • it's fine to have both, the elaborator can handle ambiguity?
  • make a typeclass? (I see this option for + and such)
The issue with finsets is that you have two natural notions of image, called docs#Finset.map and docs#Finset.image, and it's not clear which one would inherit the notation.
Looks like whenever you can use map, you can also use image (with a coercion)? Though it may indeed be more convenient to have the injectivity assumption.

One requires DecidableEq to delete the duplicates while the other doesn't:

import Mathlib

/-- info: 1 -/
#guard_msgs in
#eval ({True} : Finset Prop).map (.refl Prop) |>.card

/-- error: failed to synthesize instance of type class DecidableEq Prop -/
#guard_msgs (substring := true, whitespace := lax) in
#eval ({True} : Finset Prop).image id |>.card

Okay I see, difference in computability. Like Finite and Fintype I guess. (That said, I thought mathlib doesn't focus too much on computability, and would use noncomputable definition if it's more natural?)
I would agree that Finset.image seems more natural to inherit the notation, as it seems like Finset.image exists just for computation. You can always use classical to get the DecidableEq instance.
It's not just computability: docs#Finset.map uses an injective function.
It behaves correctly under Finset.sum, for example. If you think about it a minute, you'll see why injectivity is necessary.
